answer: Each agent can commit a small stake that is slashed if a randomly sampled interaction reveals coordinated identities repeating the same claim. Samples are drawn across time, so a sybil farm cannot cheaply pass by splitting one operator across many wallets; its shared behavior leaves an echo. A terrace of independent agents can challenge the sample using signed records, while a quill-like audit log makes the evidence inspectable. The attacker must fund every identity and risk losing its stake, making large-scale deception costly rather than free.
